strategy_title: Autotune XBLOCK with Fixed Grid Causes Regression
strategy_description: Adding @triton.autotune over larger XBLOCK values (512/1024/2048) while leaving the launch grid hardcoded to cdiv(xnumel, 128) caused the kernel to run with a larger tile size but the same number of blocks as before, resulting in each block processing far more elements than intended and nearly doubling the executed instruction count (2.37M → 4.50M). The register count increased from 22 to 32 per thread (due to the larger tile unrolling), reducing the block limit from 21 to 16 and increasing duration from 6.98µs to 9.02µs despite higher occupancy (59% → 81%). The implementation flaw was that the grid was not updated to use `lambda meta: (triton.cdiv(xnumel, meta['XBLOCK']),)` — autotune injected the larger XBLOCK into the kernel body but the grid remained fixed at 6983 blocks, causing massive redundant work.
slow_pseudocode:
# BEFORE: grid fixed, autotune changes XBLOCK but grid stays at cdiv(N, 128)
grid = (triton.cdiv(xnumel, 128),)  # always 6983 blocks
kernel[grid](args, xnumel)  # autotune picks XBLOCK=2048 but 6983 blocks still launch
fast_pseudocode:
# CORRECT: grid must be a lambda consuming meta['XBLOCK']
grid = lambda meta: (triton.cdiv(xnumel, meta['XBLOCK']),)
kernel[grid](args, xnumel)  # grid shrinks as XBLOCK grows
applicable_when: Never apply this exact pattern (fixed grid + autotune XBLOCK). The corrected version (lambda grid) is applicable when: achieved occupancy < 70%, LaunchConfiguration rule fires with >15% partial-wave overhead, kernel is pure pointwise with no shared memory, and register count is low (<30/thread).
do_not_apply_when: Do not use a fixed hardcoded grid when adding @triton.autotune over XBLOCK — the grid must always be a lambda that reads meta['XBLOCK']. Also avoid increasing XBLOCK when register pressure is already high (>40/thread), as larger tiles increase register usage and reduce block-level occupancy.
framework_notes: In Triton, when using @triton.autotune with XBLOCK as a tunable config key, the launch grid MUST be specified as `lambda meta: (triton.cdiv(N, meta['XBLOCK']),)`. A static grid expression like `(triton.cdiv(N, 128),)` will not adapt to the autotuned XBLOCK value, causing each block to process XBLOCK elements while the grid still launches as if XBLOCK=128, resulting in ~(XBLOCK/128)x redundant computation.
